stableMappingPatterns.name: effectiveDate unadjustedDate -> effectiveDate.adjustableDate.unadjustedDate
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Effective dates from FpML unadjustedDate elements are consistently copied into the CDM effectiveDate.adjustableDate.unadjustedDate slots.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Preserves the unadjusted effective date semantics; seen in multiple long- and short-form examples.
caveats: Date string normalization (timezone trimming) is applied in many examples — see normalization rules.
Some examples include additional business center or adjustedDate elements that require separate handling.

stableMappingPatterns.name: trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate -> trade.tradeDate.value
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Trade header tradeDate entries are normalized/mapped into a single trade.tradedate.value field in the CDM representation.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Consolidates trade-level date into the CDM tradeDate slot used by downstream processes.
caveats: Some mappings show reformatting of the date string (e.g., timezone removal) during the copy.

stableMappingPatterns.name: notional.notionalAmount.amount|currency -> quantity.value.value|unit.currency.value (tradeLot/priceQuantity)
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Notional amounts from FpML are relocated into CDM quantity/price representations (tradeLot or priceQuantity) preserving numeric value and currency.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM models notional as trade lot/quantity; mapping retains economic magnitude and currency semantics.
caveats: Some examples resolve equityNotionalAmount references prior to mapping (see representative highlights).

stableMappingPatterns.name: instrumentId / equity identifier -> Security.identifier / Observable identifier
stableMappingPatterns.sourcePattern: equity instrumentId / equity id and exchange (FpML)
stableMappingPatterns.targetPattern: Security.identifier or Observable.identifier with exchange metadata (CDM)
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Equity/instrument identifiers present in the FpML trades are consistently mapped into CDM security/observable identifier fields, often preserving id and exchange attributes.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM requires an observable/security identifier for equity underlyers; mapping ensures the same identifier is available in CDM for pricing and reference.
caveats: Exchange identifier normalization (FpML exchangeId -> CDM exchange code) is applied in many examples but the mapping source/rules are not explicit.

stableMappingPatterns.name: party references -> payer/receiver resolution
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Party hrefs used inside interest/leg structures are resolved to explicit payer/receiver roles in CDM payout structures.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM requires explicit counterparty role assignment for payout definitions; mapping resolves FpML hrefs to those roles.
caveats: Some examples suggest role inversion or ambiguity between Party1/Party2 mapping — verify role derivation logic per trade.

stableMappingPatterns.name: partyTradeIdentifier.versionedTradeId.tradeId -> assignedIdentifier.identifier.value
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: FpML trade identifiers are placed into CDM assignedIdentifier structures to record the trade's id value.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM uses assignedIdentifier to represent external trade ids; mapping copies the FpML tradeId into this slot.
caveats: The provenance of other meta/globalKey fields derived from FpML is not explicit and may be enriched post-mapping.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Strip trailing 'Z' timezone and normalize date format to YYYY-MM-DD
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Date strings with trailing 'Z' timezone are trimmed and reformatted to a normalized YYYY-MM-DD representation in the CDM.
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.targetSide: CDM date strings normalized to YYYY-MM-DD
notes: Representative notes: 'strip trailing Z timezone', 'normalize to YYYY-MM-DD'.
Applied to effectiveDate, terminationDate and tradeDate fields in multiple examples.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Reshape notional amount into tradeLot / quantity and priceQuantity structures
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Notional amount and currency are transformed from nested notional elements into CDM tradeLot quantity or priceQuantity value/unit structures.
notes: Ensures numeric amount and currency are retained in CDM structures used downstream for valuation.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Resolve href references to explicit Party roles (payer/receiver/party1/party2)
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: FpML href-based party references are dereferenced and mapped to explicit role fields in CDM payouts and counterparty slots.
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.sourceSide: partyReference hrefs within legs and payout structures (FpML)
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.targetSide: explicit payer/receiver or Party1/Party2 role fields (CDM)
notes: Some examples show ambiguous or inverted role assignments — verification of role-derivation logic is needed per trade.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Split separate legs into multiple payout entries
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Multiple FpML legs (e.g., separate interest/equity legs or compounding legs) are represented as separate payout objects in CDM.
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.sourceSide: Multiple leg elements in FpML trade (interestLeg, equityLeg, etc.)
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.targetSide: Multiple payout entries in CDM trade representation
notes: Leg-level semantics (rate specs, compoundingSpread) may require additional enrichment to populate CDM rateSpecification fields.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Exchange identifier normalization varies by example
variantsAndExceptions.description: FpML exchangeId values are converted to CDM exchange codes/names in several examples, but the specific mapping rules/source are inconsistent or unspecified.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Prevents a safe, deterministic rule for exchange code normalization; mapping must be driven by an external exchange code table or flagged for manual review.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Calculation agent role mapping not explicit
variantsAndExceptions.description: Mapping of FpML calculationAgentParty to CDM calculationAgent roles (e.g., 'CalculationAgentIndependent') is shown in at least one example but the rule is unclear.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Agent role derivation requires explicit rule or lookup; treat as an exception requiring confirmation or augmentation.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Payer/receiver inversion or ambiguity
variantsAndExceptions.description: Some examples indicate possible inversion or ambiguous derivation of payer vs receiver when resolving party hrefs.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Role-resolution logic must be validated per trade; do not assume a fixed Party1->payer mapping without confirming source roles.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Compounding/leg-level rate details need special handling
variantsAndExceptions.description: Elements like compoundingSpread or spreadSchedules are present but their representation in CDM rateSpecification is not consistent across examples.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: RateSpecification mapping for compounding/spread details should be treated as a specialized case and validated against domain expectations.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: Timezone trimming as normalization
suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.description: Many mappings remove trailing 'Z' from FpML date-time strings before inserting into CDM; treated as a normalization rather than a semantic change.
caution: Confirm that timezone removal is acceptable for all date fields and does not drop timezone-sensitive semantics.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: Exchange code/name enrichment
suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.description: CDM exchange codes/names (e.g., 'XPAR','NASD','XNSE','XTAI') appear in examples where FpML supplied human-readable exchange ids; likely an enrichment step using an exchange code mapping table.
caution: Mapping source is not provided; applying an exchange code lookup without an authoritative table may be incorrect.
Where exchange mapping is required, surface for review or apply a controlled mapping source.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: meta/globalKey population from FpML trade identifiers

caution: Avoid assuming full CDM meta population rules—treat as an enrichment step that needs explicit specification.
